aria: Animated recap of the Hawks' 87 to 86 win at Boston: Nickeil Alexander-Walker's driving layup with 54 seconds left that broke an 83 to 83 tie, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Jalen Johnson's 24 points and 12 rebounds, the top scorers, how the Hawks won, and the next game.

notes: Box score from Hoops Nightly's game page for the Hawks' 87–86 win at Boston on Nov 27, 2026, the last NBA Cup group game for both teams; Digest Sports matches every line. All 87 Atlanta points and all 86 Boston points add up from the player lines, as do the shooting totals (30 of 81, 11 of 45 from three, 16 of 20 FT for Atlanta; 32 of 78, 11 of 37, 11 of 16 for Boston), assists (21–14), steals (12–10) and blocks (3–5). Rebounds (37–51) are the player totals, as on Digest Sports. The quarter scores (14–25–31–17 to 29–22–18–17) are on Hoops Nightly, Digest Sports and FOX Sports; Boston led 51–39 at the half (AP) and Atlanta 70–69 after three (Roundtable Sports). Points off turnovers (26–11) are from Hoops Nightly, Field Level Media and ClutchPoints; bench points (32–25), second-chance points (6–18) and the biggest leads (Atlanta 4, Boston 17) are from Hoops Nightly, and Roundtable Sports and ClutchPoints also have Boston's 17. Boston's turnover total differs between sources (26 or 23), so it isn't used. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Friday's games.

Jalen Johnson had 24 points and 12 rebounds (Hoops Nightly; AP). Atlanta shot 28% in the first half and held Boston to 35 points in the second (AP). It was the Hawks' fifth straight win, and both teams finished group play 3–1, with Atlanta winning East Group C on the head-to-head tiebreaker (AP); Boston advanced as the East wild card (Field Level Media; ClutchPoints). Neemias Queta had a career-high 22 rebounds for Boston (AP; Field Level Media). The finish: Jalen Johnson blocked Jayson Tatum's floater with 34.5 seconds left, Dyson Daniels stole Tatum's pass with 3.8 left, Alexander-Walker made two free throws with 2.6 left for 87–83, and Derrick White's 27-foot three at the horn made it 87–86 (Hoops Nightly and Digest Sports play-by-play; AP). Next: Atlanta visits New York and Boston visits San Antonio, both on Sunday (Hoops Nightly; AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Nickeil Alexander-Walker's driving layup with 54.3 seconds left that broke an 83–83 tie, after Derrick White's floater tied it with 1:10 left: Digest Sports' play-by-play has "makes driving layup" at 0:54.3 with no assist, Hoops Nightly has the same, and the AP says he "finished a drive" with 54.3 seconds left to break the tie. So the board's Tied to Hawks +2 is 83–83 to 85–83. Where the drive started and who defended it are not described, so it is drawn as the template's plain drive to the rim. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Atlanta Hawks or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Alexander-Walker's listed 6-foot-5 and 205 pounds (Basketball-Reference; Wikipedia), with arms scaled to the 6-foot-9½ wingspan measured at the 2019 draft combine (NBADraft.net), in the Hawks' road kit with No. 7 (Basketball-Reference). He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn in the kit with the default skin tone. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
